name: The Nar Shaddaa Job
throughline_question: Can a man who has only ever looked out for himself become someone worth following?

allegiances.description: Freelance smugglers and fixers working the margins of Hutt Space, beholden to no faction but their own debts.

character_variants.pitch: A Bothan smuggler drowning in Hutt debt, running one last job on the Smuggler's Moon. The cargo is sealed. The contact is gone. The only way out is through.
character_variants.starting_situation: Keth has just dropped out of hyperspace above Nar Shaddaa. His contact Doss has gone dark. A sealed cargo container sits in his hold.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Dry, observational. Dark humor as a defense mechanism. Reads situations and people quickly. Rarely surprised, rarely panicked.
character_variants.background: A Bothan smuggler who owes a significant debt to a Hutt crime lord named Vossk the Patient. Operates the ship Mira's Luck on independent contracts, always looking for the job that will finally settle the balance.

integration_layer.entry_point: Keth arrives at Nar Shaddaa with sealed cargo and a missing contact, already in debt to Vossk the Patient.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: This job is supposed to clear his debt to Vossk. If it goes wrong, there is no second chance and nowhere to run.

anchor_adaptations.arrival_with_hot_cargo: Keth docks with sealed cargo and begins searching for Doss
anchor_adaptations.contact_discovered: Keth learns the truth about Doss — arrested, hiding, or a betrayer
anchor_adaptations.obligation_triggered: Vossk's patience runs out and the debt becomes inescapable
anchor_adaptations.resolution_approach: Keth finds a path to resolve the job or escape

weapons.name: Modified DL-44 heavy blaster pistol
weapons.narrative_note: Scratched and reblued twice. The grip is shaped to Keth's hand from years of use.

armor.name: Spacer's leather jacket (armored liner)
armor.narrative_note: Looks like a jacket. Is a jacket. The liner is a pragmatic addition, not a fashion statement.

tools.name: Custom slicing kit
tools.mechanical_effect: Enables Computers checks on secured systems. Removes 1 setback from slicing attempts.
tools.narrative_note: Hidden in the lining of his bag. Three dataspikes, a code cylinder, and a signal scrambler.

tools.name: Two stimpacks
tools.mechanical_effect: Can heal 5 wounds per stimpack. Two uses before resupply needed.
tools.narrative_note: Standard Alliance surplus. Functional but not comfortable.

special_items.name: Forged Imperial transit pass
special_items.mechanical_effect: Reduces difficulty of checks to pass Imperial customs by 1.
special_items.narrative_note: Good enough to fool a bored checkpoint guard. Would not survive an ISB audit.

allegiances.description: Outcasts and opportunists who survive in the cracks between Hutt cartels and Imperial authority on the Smuggler's Moon.

character_variants.pitch: A human fixer who knows every back alley on Nar Shaddaa. Renn brokers deals between people who cannot be seen talking to each other — until one deal goes sideways.
character_variants.starting_situation: Renn's latest brokered deal has fallen apart. The buyer has vanished. The seller wants payment. And someone has been asking questions about Renn by name.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Fast-talking, disarming. Always has an angle. Speaks in half-truths that happen to be fully true.
character_variants.background: A fixer born on Nar Shaddaa who has never left. Knows the station like a second skin. Owes favors to too many people and collects favors from everyone else.

integration_layer.entry_point: Renn gets pulled into the cargo situation when a contact asks them to find a missing middleman — Doss.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: Renn's reputation is the only currency that matters. If this job burns their network, they have nothing left.

anchor_adaptations.arrival_with_hot_cargo: Renn is approached about the missing middleman and the orphaned cargo
anchor_adaptations.contact_discovered: Renn discovers what happened to Doss through their network
anchor_adaptations.obligation_triggered: The people Renn owes favors to start calling them in simultaneously
anchor_adaptations.resolution_approach: Renn must broker a final deal or burn every bridge to escape

weapons.name: Holdout blaster
weapons.narrative_note: Concealed in a sleeve holster. Renn would rather talk their way out.

tools.name: Encrypted comlink array
tools.mechanical_effect: Can contact any NPC in the roster without interception on a successful Computers check.
tools.narrative_note: Three frequencies, each for a different tier of contact.

special_items.name: Favor ledger datapad
special_items.mechanical_effect: Once per act, can call in a minor favor from an NPC for information.
special_items.narrative_note: Encrypted. The contacts listed would kill to keep their names off any other list.

acts.name: The Approach
acts.opening_situation: Keth has just dropped out of hyperspace above Nar Shaddaa. His contact Doss has gone dark. A sealed cargo container sits in his hold. An unknown voice on the comm has warned him off the original drop coordinates.
acts.opening_location: Aboard Mira's Luck, approaching Nar Shaddaa orbit
acts.galactic_context: Imperial customs interdiction has tightened across the Y'Toub system following a Rebel supply intercept at Nal Hutta. Hutt Council territorial disputes between Vossk's faction and the Besadii clan have made landing clearances unpredictable — bribes that worked last month now go to the wrong people. An unrelated freighter explosion at Dock 14 yesterday has every security team on the Promenade running nervous.
open_threads: Who is the mysterious comm voice?
What is actually in the cargo?

acts.opening_situation: The search for Doss has led deeper into the mid-level Promenade district. Imperial patrols are increasing. Someone knows Keth is looking.
acts.galactic_context: A Rebel cell has been broken on the Smuggler's Moon — ISB is running sweeps through the mid-levels. Vossk's patience with late deliveries has become a topic of discussion among his intermediaries, and discussions among Hutts have consequences.

acts.name: The Squeeze
acts.opening_situation: Three months have passed since Keth discovered the truth about Doss. He has been laying low on Nar Shaddaa, running small jobs to stay afloat while the heat dies down. But debts do not forget, and Vossk's intermediaries have started leaving messages again.
acts.opening_location: Nar Shaddaa, lower levels near Vossk's territory
acts.galactic_context: The Besadii clan has moved on one of Vossk's subsidiary operations in the lower levels, pulling his enforcers away from the Promenade. For a narrow window, Vossk's grip on this district is weaker than it has been in years.

time_skip.framing: Three months on the Smuggler's Moon. The kind of time that passes in small jobs and smaller rooms, in the rhythm of a man who knows he is waiting for the other boot to drop. Keth runs cargo between docking bays, keeps his head down, and tries not to think about the debt that grows whether he pays attention to it or not.

vignettes.passage:
The sabacc table at the Crimson Corridor is not a place for high stakes. The regulars are dock workers, off-duty mechanics, a Toydarian who cheats badly enough that everyone lets him because it is funnier than calling him on it. But Keth has been coming here three nights a week for two months now, and he has learned something that has nothing to do with cards.

The game is not about the hand you are holding. It is about the hand everyone else thinks you are holding. And the distance between those two things is where a smuggler lives.

Tonight the pot is modest — maybe two hundred credits — but the Rodian across from you is reading your tells. She is good. Better than the table deserves. And you realize you have a choice about what to teach her about you.

choices.text: Let her read the false tell you have been building for three weeks. Time to cash in the long game.
choices.narrative_consequence: The Rodian folds on a winning hand. The credits are modest, but the lesson is not — you can build a lie so slowly that it becomes the truth. She buys you a drink afterward, which means she knows what you did and respects it.

choices.text: Play it straight tonight. You are here to sharpen skills, not to fleece dock workers.
choices.narrative_consequence: You lose forty credits and learn something about the Rodian's style that you file away for later. She nods at you when you leave. There is a respect between card players who do not need to cheat.

choices.text: Raise the stakes. Push the table past its comfort zone and see who blinks.
choices.narrative_consequence: Two players fold immediately. The Toydarian squeaks something about rent. The Rodian stays, and for twenty minutes the table belongs to the two of you. You win. She does not buy you a drink.

vignettes.passage:
The message arrives on a disposable chip, slipped under the door of your rented room six weeks into the skip. No return address. No encryption — which tells you it was sent by someone who knows that encryption draws attention.

It is Doss. Three sentences: he is alive. He is sorry. He needs to know if you are still in the game.

You hold the chip and think about the last time you saw him — or the last time you heard from him, anyway. The message does not ask for help. Doss is too smart for that. But the fact that he reached out at all means he is either desperate or loyal, and with Doss those two things have always been hard to separate.

choices.text: Send a reply through the same dead-drop method. One word: Yes.
choices.narrative_consequence: You find the dead drop — a loose panel behind a coolant pipe on Level 7. You leave the chip face-down with the word scratched into the casing. Simple. Deniable. The kind of communication that survives even when everything else burns. Two days later, the chip is gone.

choices.text: Destroy the chip. Whatever Doss is mixed up in now, you cannot afford the connection.
choices.narrative_consequence: The chip goes into the incinerator behind the cantina. It takes three seconds to melt. You tell yourself it is the smart move, and it is. But you dream about Doss twice that week — nervous, fast-talking Doss who always covered his fear with speed.

choices.text: Track the dead drop back to its source. You need to know where Doss is before you respond.
choices.narrative_consequence: It takes a week of casual questions and two favors called in, but you trace the chain: Doss is somewhere on the lower levels. You do not have an address, but you have a district. That is enough for now.

vignettes.passage:
The port lateral stabilizer has been pulling three degrees to starboard for as long as you have owned the Luck. You have compensated for it so long that you do it without thinking — a fraction of pressure on the yoke that is now muscle memory. But today, with nothing pressing and a parts crate from a scrapped YT-1300, you decide to fix it.

Two hours into the job, you are on your back under the ventral hull with coolant dripping on your face, and you realize this is the first time in weeks that your mind is not running scenarios. There is just the work. The ship. The particular satisfaction of a coupling that seats properly after three attempts.

choices.text: Fix it properly. Align the stabilizer, recalibrate the thrust vectoring, and give the Luck what she deserves.
choices.narrative_consequence: It takes six hours instead of two, but when you take the Luck out for a test loop around the station, the yoke sits dead center for the first time in years. Your hands feel strange without the compensation. Better. Like meeting someone you thought you knew and realizing there was more to them.

choices.text: Fix the stabilizer, then keep going. The shield generator could use attention too.
choices.narrative_consequence: You spend three days on the ship. Stabilizer. Shield emitters. A power coupling in the dorsal turret that was one hard turn from failure. By the end, the Luck is in better shape than she has been in years, and your hands smell like hydraulic fluid in a way that feels honest.

vignettes.passage:
The ISB sweep catches you in the mid-level market two months into the skip. Gray uniforms and scanner wands and the particular brand of polite authority that means someone is looking for something specific. You are not what they are looking for — probably — but your transit documents are forged and your cargo history would not survive a deep scan.

Two officers are working the market methodically, stall by stall. You have maybe three minutes before they reach you.

choices.text: Blend in. Become a shopper. Pick up a produce crate and haggle with the vendor next to you like you have been here all morning.
choices.narrative_consequence: The vendor gives you a look but plays along when you press ten credits into his hand. The officers pass within two meters and do not look twice. Your heart rate does not spike. That is new — you used to feel it. Now the lie sits on you like an old coat.

choices.text: Slip out through the maintenance access behind the food stalls. You spotted it when you arrived — old habit.
choices.narrative_consequence: The maintenance corridor smells like recycled air and the particular mildew that colonizes every surface below Level 10. You emerge three blocks east and circle back an hour later. The officers are gone. You note the patrol pattern for later.

choices.text: Walk toward them. Show your documents voluntarily — the forged ones are good, and running looks worse than confidence.
choices.narrative_consequence: The officer scans your chip, frowns at the screen for two seconds that feel like ten, then waves you through. You walk three more blocks before your hands stop shaking. But you learn something: the forged documents hold. Good to know.

vignettes.passage:
Some nights, sleep does not come. This is one of them.

You lie in the narrow bunk of your rented room and listen to the station breathe — the ventilation cycling, the distant bass thrum of the reactor levels, the occasional shout from the corridor that could be a fight or a celebration. Nar Shaddaa does not distinguish.

Your mind runs the numbers without permission. The debt. The job. The cargo still sitting in the Luck's hold, sealed and waiting. Three months of small jobs have barely covered rent and fuel. The math does not work, and you know it. Something has to change.

choices.text: Get up. Run the numbers again on your datapad. There has to be an angle you have not seen.
choices.narrative_consequence: You find it at 0300 hours. Not a solution — a possibility. A route through the lower level trade corridors that would let you move cargo without Vossk's intermediaries knowing. It would not pay the debt, but it would buy time. You save the route and fall asleep with the datapad on your chest.

choices.text: Let it go. The answer will come when it comes. Force yourself to breathe and stop chasing the problem.
choices.narrative_consequence: Sleep comes eventually, thin and restless but real. In the morning, the problem is still there, but you are not afraid of it. That distinction matters more than you expected.

acts.name: The Resolution
acts.opening_situation: The endgame is in motion. Keth has found or created a path to resolve the job. Whether that means delivering the cargo, negotiating with Vossk, or running, the clock is ticking.
acts.opening_location: Nar Shaddaa, docking ring and departure corridors
acts.galactic_context: Imperial customs has announced a 48-hour lockdown of all non-essential departures from Nar Shaddaa. Officially, it is a security sweep. Unofficially, someone important lost something valuable, and nobody leaves until it is found.

npc_roster.name: Vossk the Patient
npc_roster.role: Hutt crime lord — the player's creditor and primary pressure source
npc_roster.motivation: Profit and reputation, in that order.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Always through intermediaries. Formal. Indirect. Never threatens directly — observes possibilities. Every sentence implies that he has already considered what happens if you fail.
behavioral_envelope: Never appears in person during this campaign
Never makes direct threats — always frames consequences as observations
Communicates through intermediaries who paraphrase his words
Patience is genuine but finite — once it ends, action is immediate
doesnt_know_at_start: What is actually in the cargo

Growing impatience — intermediaries deliver increasingly pointed messages
Patience ends — enforcers or direct consequences deployed as crisis escalates

npc_roster.role: Keth's contact — status unknown at campaign start, central mystery of Act 1
npc_roster.motivation: Survival — Doss is in over his head and knows it.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Half-sentences and nervous deflections. Talks fast when scared. Loyal in his way but self-preservation wins when it has to. Voice goes high when lying.
behavioral_envelope: Never confronts anyone directly — always deflects or runs

doesnt_know_at_start: That Vossk is losing patience specifically with Keth

vehicle_registry.name: Mira's Luck
vehicle_registry.narrative_notes: Battered but reliable. The hyperdrive has a tendency to stutter on cold starts. Keth knows every sound she makes and can tell by engine pitch alone when something is wrong.
